preconditions.expression: all(2 <= n <= 10**5 for line in stdin.splitlines() if line.strip().isdigit() and int(line.strip()) == n)
preconditions.description: Each test case starts with an integer n (2 ≤ n ≤ 10^5) representing the number of vertices in the tree.

preconditions.expression: all(len(edges) == n - 1 for n, edges in [(int(stdin.splitlines()[i]), [tuple(map(int, line.split())) for line in stdin.splitlines()[i+1:i+n]]) for i in range(1, len(stdin.splitlines()), n+1)])
preconditions.description: Each test case contains exactly n-1 edges describing an unweighted tree with n vertices.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= a <= n and 1 <= b <= n and a != b for n, edges in [(int(stdin.splitlines()[i]), [tuple(map(int, line.split())) for line in stdin.splitlines()[i+1:i+n]]) for i in range(1, len(stdin.splitlines()), n+1)] for a, b in edges)
preconditions.description: Each edge (a_i, b_i) connects two distinct vertices within the range [1, n].

preconditions.expression: all(len(stdin.splitlines()) == 1 + sum(int(stdin.splitlines()[i]) for i in range(0, len(stdin.splitlines()), int(stdin.splitlines()[i]) + 1)))
preconditions.description: The input format is correct: t test cases, each with n followed by n-1 edges.

postconditions.expression: all(len(output_lines) == 2 * k + 1 for k, output_lines in [(int(line) if line.strip().isdigit() else None for line in stdout.splitlines()) for line in stdout.splitlines() if line.strip().isdigit()])
postconditions.description: For each test case, the first line of output is an integer k (the minimum number of operations), followed by exactly k lines of 4 integers each (x1, y1, x2, y2) representing the operations.

postconditions.expression: all(1 <= x1 <= n and 1 <= y1 <= n and x1 != y1 and 1 <= x2 <= n and 1 <= y2 <= n and x2 != y2 for n, edges, k, ops in [(int(stdin.splitlines()[i]), [tuple(map(int, line.split())) for line in stdin.splitlines()[i+1:i+n]], int(stdout.splitlines()[j]), [tuple(map(int, line.split())) for line in stdout.splitlines()[j+1:j+k+1]]) for i, j in [(0, 0), (1 + n, 1 + n + 1)]])
postconditions.description: Each operation (x1, y1, x2, y2) has valid vertex indices (1 ≤ x1, y1, x2, y2 ≤ n) and x1 ≠ y1, x2 ≠ y2.

postconditions.expression: all((x1, y1) in edges or (y1, x1) in edges for n, edges, k, ops in [(int(stdin.splitlines()[i]), [tuple(map(int, line.split())) for line in stdin.splitlines()[i+1:i+n]], int(stdout.splitlines()[j]), [tuple(map(int, line.split())) for line in stdout.splitlines()[j+1:j+k+1]]) for i, j in [(0, 0), (1 + n, 1 + n + 1)]] for (x1, y1, x2, y2) in ops)
postconditions.description: The edge (x1, y1) being removed must exist in the original tree (or be present at the time of removal, but the problem allows any order of operations).

postconditions.expression: all(is_bamboo(n, edges, ops) for n, edges, k, ops in [(int(stdin.splitlines()[i]), [tuple(map(int, line.split())) for line in stdin.splitlines()[i+1:i+n]], int(stdout.splitlines()[j]), [tuple(map(int, line.split())) for line in stdout.splitlines()[j+1:j+k+1]]) for i, j in [(0, 0), (1 + n, 1 + n + 1)]])
postconditions.description: After performing all k operations, the resulting graph is a bamboo (a tree where no node has degree > 2).

postconditions.expression: all(k == min_operations(n, edges) for n, edges, k, ops in [(int(stdin.splitlines()[i]), [tuple(map(int, line.split())) for line in stdin.splitlines()[i+1:i+n]], int(stdout.splitlines()[j]), [tuple(map(int, line.split())) for line in stdout.splitlines()[j+1:j+k+1]]) for i, j in [(0, 0), (1 + n, 1 + n + 1)]])
postconditions.description: The value k is the minimum number of operations required to transform the original tree into a bamboo.
